items.q: When is Festival of Lights Berlin 2026?
items.a: **October 9–18, 2026**, under the motto **Colours of Love**. The official programme lists 37 illuminated locations.

items.q: What time are the outdoor illuminations on?
items.a: Normally **19:00–23:00 (7–11 pm)**. Individual installations can have different dates or hours; check the official location page for your evening.

items.q: Is Festival of Lights Berlin free?
items.a: The **outdoor light walk is free**. Indoor shows, concerts and special tours need separate tickets. Beyond the Light inside Berlin Cathedral runs October 9–11 (€28); In Concert runs October 13–17 (from €58). Check availability for the exact slot.

items.q: What is the best central walking route?
items.a: Start at **Alexanderplatz**, then walk through the Nikolai Quarter, Berlin Cathedral, Bebelplatz and Brandenburg Gate to **Potsdamer Platz**. Allow 2 to 2.5 hours for a few complete shows and photo stops; seeing every work takes longer.

items.q: How long should I stay at each projection?
items.a: Approximate programme lengths are **TV Tower 10 minutes, Rathausstraße 17 4, Berlin Cathedral 6, Humboldt University 6, Hotel de Rome & Behren Palais 12, Brandenburg Gate 10 and Kollhoff Tower 5**. Wait for a complete loop.
**Konzerthaus has no festival show on October 11. The park at Rathaus Lichtenberg is illuminated only on October 9.** Check each official location page before travelling.

items.q: Where can I see the Pergamonmuseum projection?
items.a: The organiser recommends **Monbijoupark across the Spree** for the approximately three-minute projection at the future interim entrance. The museum itself remains closed.

items.q: How can I combine the festival with a daytime walking tour?
items.a: My **Berlin Then and Now walking tour** starts at the World Clock on Alexanderplatz and lasts about 2.5 hours. Check available dates on the booking page, then plan the festival as a separate evening walk.
